description: What people *do* with a plant, declared once so that a use is a value rather than whatever the author typed that afternoon. The last free-text vocabulary in canon: `culture`, `species`, `clade`, `growth_form`, `material_class` and `affordance` were all declared before it, and `uses` was left because the making layer had a better reason to leave it than to fold it in.
note:
**This is not `material_classes.json`, and the difference is why it survived that work.** A material class says what you can carry away -- fibre, timber, resin. A use says what the plant is *for*, and more than half of these are not substances at all: you cannot carry away shade, or a boundary, or a tree you steer by. Folding the two together would have destroyed a distinction rather than declared one, so `uses` stayed where it was and is declared here on its own terms.

The numbers are what an undeclared vocabulary looks like: 51 distinct values across 59 uses on 27 plants, and 44 of the 51 appeared exactly once. `ritual`, `ritual_offering` and `ritual_wood` were three values for one idea; `food`, `fruit`, `staple_food`, `staple_grain` and `flood_crop` were five. Nothing was wrong with any of them individually, which is exactly how this happens.

Distinctions are kept where they are real, on the ruling `species.json` already carries: declaring a vocabulary is about catching the twenty-second value typed by accident, not about flattening twenty-one real ideas into eight. `memory` stays apart from `ritual` because canon's oracle fig genuinely stores a record, and `shade` stays apart from everything because a tree you sit under is doing something no substance does.

food.label: Food
food.note: Eaten as a staple or grown as a crop. Absorbed `fruit`, `staple_food`, `staple_grain` and `flood_crop` -- the last of which is a fact about *when* it is grown and belongs in the plant's notes, not in a use.

seasoning.label: Seasoning
seasoning.note: Changes the taste of other food rather than being the meal. Pepper and tamarind. Held apart from `food` because a delta that has one and not the other is in real trouble in a way the word `food` hides.

drink.label: Drink
drink.note: Brewed, steeped or fermented. Canon's mahua and its black ash-tea.

psychoactive.label: Psychoactive
psychoactive.note: Changes the mind. A stimulant and a dream-inducer are the same category read at two strengths, and neither is medicine -- filing them under `physic` would have canon claiming the Blood-red Asura Lotus is a treatment.

physic.label: Physic
physic.note: Treats a hurt or a sickness. Absorbed `medicine`, `wound_salve`, `tonic`, `insect_repellent` and `household_herb` -- the last because a herb kept by the door is kept to be used.

poison.label: Poison
poison.note: Harms, and is known to. Its own value rather than a negative `physic`, because a culture that plants oleander on a boundary is using the harm on purpose.

timber.label: Timber
timber.note: Wood cut for structure. Absorbed `construction`, `ship_timber`, `tower_beams`, `scaffolding` and `rafts`, which are five things one plank does.

craftwork.label: Craftwork
craftwork.note: Worked into small objects rather than into a building. A sandalwood comb is not timber, and canon lists `carving` and `tools` separately for exactly that reason.

fibre.label: Fibre
fibre.note: Spun, woven or thatched. Absorbed `thatching` and `mat_weaving`, which are one fibre at two scales.

fuel.label: Fuel
fuel.note: Burnt for heat. Canon has one -- the ghost mangrove, for charcoal.

fragrance.label: Fragrance
fragrance.note: Burnt or worn for its scent. Absorbed `incense` and `perfume`, which differ in how they are used and not in what the plant is for.

trade.label: Trade
trade.note: Carried and sold beyond where it grows. Says a plant has worth without canon committing to a price, exactly as the `trade` affordance does for objects. Absorbed `trade_resin`, which said the same thing twice.

ritual.label: Ritual
ritual.note: Used in observance. Absorbed `ritual_offering`, `ritual_wood` and `omen_reading` -- three values for the same idea, which is what an undeclared vocabulary produces.

memory.label: Memory
memory.note: The plant holds a record. Kept apart from `ritual` because canon means it literally: the Silver-Leaved Oracle Fig is an archive and the moonseed vine is grafted onto one. If that ever turns out to be metaphor, this is the value that should go.

shade.label: Shade
shade.note: Stood or sat under. The most common use in canon and the one that proves this file is not `material_classes.json` -- there is nothing here to carry away.

ornament.label: Ornament
ornament.note: Grown to be looked at. Absorbed `decorative`.

boundary.label: Boundary
boundary.note: Marks or bars a line. Absorbed `barrier_hedge`, `boundary_marker` and `warning_marker`: a hedge that stops you and a hedge that warns you are the same hedge doing its job at two distances.

landmark.label: Landmark
landmark.note: Steered by. The ghost mangrove marks a channel, which is a use even though nobody touches the tree.

filtration.label: Filtration
filtration.note: Cleans water or binds what is dissolved in it. Absorbed `mineral_filter`, `filter_beds` and `mineral_binder`. The emerald harbour lotus and the saltreed both do it, at opposite ends of the delta.
